files: /mnt/project-files/history/tools/slug.py (written by another builder first; imported, not changed)
problems: Slug collision: "Han" (-404..-203) and "Hán" (-206..-204) both slugify to `han`; the table gives the later one `han-2` (earlier first_year keeps the bare slug). Any builder deriving a slug from a Name must check polities.csv for this; shape_ids follow (han-2_-206).

Cliopatria has no "United Kingdom" Name: the British state 1709..2024 is "Kingdom of Great Britain"; its union-based modern_countries is Oman;Yemen;United Kingdom because Arabian-era shapes carry that Name.

Polity-level modern_countries ranks by overlap with the union of all shapes, so former territory dominates for states that shrank (French Fifth Republic -> Algeria, State of Israel -> Egypt, Republic of China -> China, Sultanate of Brunei -> Philippines, Netherlands Antilles -> Suriname, Mujahideen -> Afghanistan); per-shape modern_countries in shapes.csv and the dossiers give the per-year answer. README lists the 7 affected polities alive in 2024.

Cliopatria row errors found while checking the join: "Estado Novo" runs 1926..2024 and its 2024 shape is a 6,900 km2 patch at Cabinda (Portugal has no shape of record after 1925 except via Estado Novo and (Portuguese Empire)); "Saint Kitts" 1967..2024 is a polygon on Saint Croix (US Virgin Islands); "Mujahideen" 1987..2024 jumps from Afghanistan to Syria/Iraq; Monaco polygons are 94 km2 for a 2 km2 state.

Impossible year ranges (one Name reused across successive states): Later Zhou -750..960, Kingdom of Italy 587..1946, Georgia 567..2024, Elam -3200..-601, Chámpa 207..1652, Zapotec Civilization -500..895, Anurādhapura -291..1017, Papal States 755..1870, Swiss Confederation 1294..2024, Kingdom of Sweden 980..2024; 71 Names span 600+ years (full list in README).

115 Wikidata ids are shared by two or more leaf Names (e.g. Q12536 Abbasid Caliphate / Abbasid Caliphate/Buyid Dynasty / Buyid Dynasty; Q12544 Eastern Roman Empire / Roman Empire; Q148 People's Republic of China / Republic of China; Q423 both Koreas; Q41137 Assyria / Syria; Q1068371 Chauhan Dynasty / Han Dynasty), and 74 groups of Names differ only by generic words; two Names carry more than one Wikidata id ((Personal union of Kingdom of Hungary with Kingdom of Bohemia), Scandinavian minor kingdoms); Timurid Empire and (Allegiance of East Franks to Carolingian Empire) have features missing Wikipedia/Wikidata.

105 leaf Names are dynasties and 16 are houses, parties or people (House of Habsburg, House of Savoy, Harsha's Empire, Samo's Empire, Trưng sisters, Chinese Communists, Danish Magnates, Spanish Nationalists); aggregates carried as leaf polities: Holy Roman Empire Minor States, Khanates of the Caucasus, Scandinavian minor kingdoms, Gaza/Hamas, Russian-occupied territories, British Overseas Territories; names with a slash: Abbasid Caliphate/Buyid Dynasty, Gaza/Hamas.

Modern countries whose Cliopatria Name differs from the Natural Earth ADMIN name: 123 of the 192 polities alive in 2024 (mostly "Republic of X" / "Kingdom of X" vs "X"; also Russian Federation vs Russia, Czech Republic vs Czechia, Union of Myanmar vs Myanmar, Republic of Côte d'Ivoire vs Ivory Coast, Éire vs Ireland, Eswatini vs eSwatini, Tanzania and Micronesia match NE's NAME field but not ADMIN); full list in README. Modern country names in all outputs are the NE ADMIN field; NAME differs from ADMIN for 64 of 258 NE features.

427 gaps of more than one year between consecutive shapes of the same Name (no shape of record for those years; the compiler must decide whether to hold or drop); 21 shapes under 100 km2 (Mercia 884..925 at 44 km2, Hunnic Empire 633..673 at 46 km2, San Marino, Monaco, Amalfi) and 237 under 1000 km2.

13 features (Kingdom of England 947, Kingdom of France 1260..1375 umbrella shapes) have invalid geometry (components with too few points), repaired with make_valid before measuring; no feature pairs of one Name overlap in time and none share a FromYear, so no b/c suffixes were needed.

Relation entities' Components list the whole membership of the larger party (27 names under (Allegiance of Swiss Confederation to Holy Roman Empire)), so parties are parsed from the Name and Components are used only for umbrella entities; all 50 relation Names resolved both parties. Where a party exists only as an umbrella (British Empire for Hawaii) the counterpart slug is the rel- slug.

Neighbour test is in degrees with the tolerance scaled by cos(latitude): exact east-west, lenient north-south (up to 25/cos(lat) km), so nothing within 25 km is missed but a few slightly farther north-south pairs are included; centroids are plain lon/lat centroids and can fall in the gap for antimeridian-straddling shapes.
polity-table.summary: Built the Cliopatria polity and shape tables. tools/build_tables.py (re-runnable, 193 s, under 2 GB RAM) loads the 173 MB GeoJSON once, repairs 13 invalid geometries, joins every shape and every polity's shape union to Natural Earth 10m admin-0 countries (ADMIN names, spherical overlap areas via a Lambert equal-area projection that reproduces Cliopatria's Area field to 0.5%), parses the 50 relation Names (allegiance 20, alliance 12, personal union 12, vassalage 6) and 43 umbrella entities' Components/MemberOf into directed relations, and finds neighbours within 25 km in overlapping years with an STRtree (17,402 symmetric entries). Outputs on the mount: data/polities.csv (1,637 rows: 1,544 leaf polities + 93 parenthesised entities), data/shapes.csv (13,797 rows, shape_id = slug_FromYear, no suffixes needed), data/polities/<slug>.json for all 1,544 leaf polities (shapes, relations with role and source, neighbours with merged year spans), and data/README.md with columns, counts, conventions and the quality issues. 1,468 leaf polities have at least one neighbour; 325 have a parsed relation. Validation: all slugs unique (one collision Han/Hán resolved as han/han-2), every shape slug, relation target and neighbour slug resolves, neighbours symmetric, no empty modern_countries; mount copies verified identical to the staged files. slug.py had been written by another builder minutes earlier with the identical rule and is imported unchanged. Key data problems for the research agents: no "United Kingdom" Name (it is "Kingdom of Great Britain" to 2024), Estado Novo to 2024 ending at Cabinda, Saint Kitts drawn on Saint Croix, Mujahideen spanning Afghanistan to Syria, 71 Names spanning 600+ years (Later Zhou, Kingdom of Italy, Georgia, Elam), 115 Wikidata ids shared across leaf Names, 105 dynasty Names, 123 modern Names differing from Natural Earth ADMIN, and union-based modern_countries over-weighting lost territory for 7 present-day states.

research-groups.summary: Wrote data/research-groups.json (76 groups, plan order, ids eu-01..eu-22, me-01..me-10, ea-01..ea-08, ia-01..ia-03, jk-01..jk-02, sa-01..sa-06, se-01..se-04, af-01..af-08, am-01..am-08, oc-01..oc-02, xx-01..xx-03; each with region, name as in the plan, era_from/era_to, a two-sentence scope naming what the agent researches and what Cliopatria lacks there, polities[] and context[]) and data/research-groups.md (table: id, name, era, owned (leaf), context, five largest by max_area_km2, plus the over-45 and zero-owned lists). All 1,637 Names in polities.csv (1,544 leaf + 93 umbrella/relation) are owned by exactly one group; unassigned = 0. Generator is tools/research_groups.py (python3 -I; explicit override table of about 1,050 slugs for historical judgment, region/era rules from modern_countries, centroid and first_year for the rest; umbrella entities go to the group of their main component: the subject of an Allegiance/Vassalage, the first party of an alliance or personal union, the same-named leaf, with 9 explicit overrides such as (Spanish Empire) and (Portuguese Empire) to eu-12 via the metropole and (Commonwealth of Nations) to eu-22). Context = polities of other groups that are 25 km neighbours (data/polities/<slug>.json neighbours[]) of an owned polity in an overlapping year of the group's era; xx-01 lists the five polities founded by 2500 BCE; xx-02 and xx-03 own nothing and have empty context by design. Judgment calls applied as instructed: Kush, Axum, Nubia, Ethiopia to af-01; Assyria, Babylon to me-02; Hittites, Mitanni, Phrygia, Lydia, Tabal, Neo-Hittites and Iron Age South Arabia to me-04; Pontus, Bithynia, Pergamon, Cappadocia, Galatia, Sophene, Ptolemies, Seleucids, Greco-Bactrians, Indo-Greeks, Judea, Nabataea, Cyrenaica to me-05; Urartu, Armenia, Colchis, Iberia, Albania, Georgia and its successors, Shirvan, the khanates, the 1918 and 1991 republics and Chechnya to eu-19; Macedonian Empire to eu-02 (eu-01 lists it as context); Scythia, Khazars, Old Great Bulgaria, Oghuz, Cumans, Kidarites, Xionites, White Huns and the Tarim states to ia-01; Ilkhanate, Timurids, Golden Horde fragments (Kazan, Astrakhan, Crimea, Sibir, Nogai, Qasim) to ia-02; Kazakh Khanate, Shaybanids, Khiva, Kalmyks, Dzungars, Mongolia 1912 onward and all Afghan states to ia-03; Tibetan Empire and Tibetans to ea-04, Tibet 1363-1952 to ea-06 by founding era; Vietnam's Nanyue to ea-02; colonial entities in India (Portuguese/Dutch/British Ceylon, French and Danish India, Company Raj, Portuguese colonies) to sa-06; maritime SE Asian states founded after 1700 (Yogyakarta, Surakarta, Malay and Bornean sultanates) to se-03 as colonial-era protectorates; European states whose Cliopatria shape is a colony (French First Republic, Batavian Republic, Portuguese Republic, Estado Novo, Vichy, Free French, Fourth and Fifth Republics) to their European era groups; Napoleonic Batavia Cape to af-07; spanning-era names (Kingdom of Italy 587-1946 to eu-13, Kingdom of Sweden 980-2024 to eu-14, Swiss Confederation to eu-09, Kingdom of Great Britain 1709-2024 and British Colonial Empire to eu-11, Rattanakosin to se-01, Burma 1820-1989 to se-01, Ethiopia 1942 to af-01, Morocco 1670 to af-02, Liberia to af-04) go to the group of their founding era or lineage, with later groups listing them as context. Balance: 76 groups; owned per group min 0, median 17.5, max 91 (leaf-only max 81). Eight groups exceed 45 and are reported rather than re-split: eu-20 Europe 1789-1914 (91; the 1803-1806 German electorates, kingdoms and duchies, the Napoleonic satellites and the French regimes), am-08 The republics from 1810 (68; all of Latin America and the Caribbean after 1804), af-08 Partition and independence (67; the colonial empires' African shapes and 53 post-1950 states), eu-12 Iberia and the taifas (61; 23 taifas), me-10 Ottomans and the modern Middle East (56; Ottomans, five Iranian dynasties, Egypt from Muhammad Ali, Gulf, Arabian and Levantine states), me-09 Turks, Crusaders, Mamluks (48 incl. 4 umbrellas; 14 beyliks and 7 post-Ilkhanid Iranian dynasties), eu-11 (47 incl. 4 umbrellas) and eu-22 (47 incl. 3 umbrellas). Eleven groups own 3 or fewer: me-07 (3), ea-06 Yuan (2), ea-07 Ming (3), af-05 Swahili (2), af-06 Central Africa (2), am-02 Maya (3), am-05 North America (3), oc-01 Polynesia (3), and xx-01/02/03 (0); their scopes say what to add. Shared-folder rule followed: both data files read back unchanged (md5 verified) after the write; my stray research_groups .pyc removed from tools/__pycache__; slug.py untouched; scratch (per-region listings, neighbour cache) under /tmp/claude-0/work/research-groups/.
problems: Eight groups own more than 45 because the plan's split forces it (counts include umbrella entities): eu-20 Europe 1789-1914 = 91 (81 leaf; 43 of them are German states founded 1803-1820 plus Napoleonic satellites and French regimes; a sub-brief 'German states 1806-1871' would bring it under 45), am-08 The republics from 1810 = 68 (one agent for all Latin America and the Caribbean after 1804; a Mexico-Central America-Caribbean / South America split would give 35 and 33), af-08 Partition and independence = 67 (53 are post-1950 states), eu-12 Iberia and the taifas = 61 (23 taifas), me-10 Ottomans and the modern Middle East = 56, me-09 Turks, Crusaders, Mamluks = 48, eu-11 = 47 and eu-22 = 47 (44 leaf each). Not re-split; reported here as asked.

The Americas are badly unbalanced by Cliopatria's coverage: the six pre-1810 groups together own 27 polities (am-01 4, am-02 3, am-03 5, am-04 4, am-05 3, am-06 8) while am-08 owns 68; ea-06 Yuan owns 2 (Yuan dynasty, Tibet 1363-1952), af-05 and af-06 own 2 each, oc-01 owns 2 leaf polities (Hawaii, Cakobau's Fiji). These agents' work is mostly addition, as their scopes say.

Some Cliopatria entities sit oddly and were placed by judgment, flagged for the dossier authors: 'hashemite-arab-federation' dated 1415-1439 in Iraq (me-09); 'mahdids' 1169-1506 centred on Oman (me-09); 'hamdanid-emirates' 936-1259 with a centroid in Pakistan/Iran (me-08); 'ptolemaic-kingdom' whose largest shape is 4.8M km2 centred in Iran (me-05); 'french-india' whose shape is the Mascarenes (sa-06); 'maynila' 1521-1599 with a Ryukyu centroid (se-02); 'new-caledonia' 1856-1859 centred in Borneo (oc-02); 'protectorate-of-the-western-regions' dated 117-601 (ea-02); 'kingdom-of-fiji' listed in the S America roster (oc-01); 'kingdom-of-great-britain' 1709-2024 and 'british-colonial-empire' 1706-1999 both go to eu-11 by founding era so eu-20/21/22 see modern Britain only as context, likewise Kingdom of Sweden 980-2024 (eu-14), Kingdom of Italy 587-1946 (eu-13), Georgia 567-2024 (eu-19), Later Zhou -750..960 (ea-01), Khmer Empire 800-1867 (se-01); the research agents must split these reused Names into one dossier per state as data/README.md already notes.

Umbrella/relation entities went to the subject or first-named party: alliances such as (Alliance between Han Dynasty and Xiongnu) to ea-02 and (Alliance between Sasanian Empire and Byzantine Empire) to me-06; the other party's group only sees them through context. If the orchestrator prefers both parties to receive relation entities, that is a one-line change in tools/research_groups.py.

Context lists use the 25 km neighbour relation from data/polities/<slug>.json, so world-spanning shapes (british-colonial-empire, british-africa, russian-empire, spanish-empire) appear as context for many distant groups; me-10 has 157 context slugs and eu-09 129. me-01 and ea-01 have empty context because no other polity comes within 25 km in their eras; oc-01 has none for the same reason.

Scope sentences name what Cliopatria lacks from general knowledge, not from pages opened; the research agents verify them against sources. The era bounds (era_from/era_to) are working bounds chosen here, not from the plan, e.g. eu-06 starts at 30 CE to hold the early Goths, eu-07 at 238 for the Rhine Franks, ia-01 at 800 BCE for Scythia, af-08 at 1830 for French Algeria, sa-06 at 1505 for Portuguese Ceylon, se-03 at 1511 for Malacca.

The first full run took 3 minutes because it downloads the 1,544 polity JSONs for the neighbour lists; they are cached at /tmp/claude-0/work/research-groups/neighbours.json and later runs take seconds. If the cache is lost and data/polities/ is missing, the script falls back to bbox proximity from shapes.csv.

grid.summary:
TASK grid done. tools/slug.py written (nobody had it; tested on the four examples). tools/grid.py provides land_cells(res=5) (Natural Earth 50m land, clipped north of 60 S, antimeridian/over-180 polygons unwrapped and split, cached sorted in data/grid/land_r5.txt and loaded as cell->index), shape_cells(geometry) (h3.geo_to_cells per split polygon plus the centroid cell of the largest part when the shape is smaller than one cell or yields no cell), polity_cells(slug, year, land_only=False) through a parsed-feature pickle (65 MB) and per-shape .npy cell caches under /tmp/claude-0/work/grid/ (177 MB, nothing on the mount), cells_to_geojson(cells, decimals=None) via h3.cells_to_h3shape with antimeridian splitting, plus anchor_name/anchor_year, to_runs/from_runs, features_alive. tools/compile_anchors.py compiles every anchor; tools/preview.py is the display test.

Land grid: 524,441 res-5 cells = 524,019 with centre on land + 422 island centroid cells (429 listed in land_r5_island_cells.txt; an NE island with no cell centre on it keeps its centroid cell so Mahe, St Croix, atolls exist). Sum of h3.cell_area = 134.3 M km2, i.e. Earth's land minus Antarctica; the master plan's 214,699 is a 2.4x undercount. Lakes are land (ne_50m_land has no lake holes); the Caspian is a hole.

Anchors: 120 files data/anchors/{m6000..m0100,p0000..p1600 by 100, p1610..p2020 by 10, p2024}.json, naming m<abs year 4 digits> for BCE and p<year> for CE (documented in data/grid/README.md); 26 anchors before -3400 have empty owners. Format {"year","grid","land_cells","owners":{slug:[runs of land_r5 indices]},"polities","cells_owned","conflicts","conflict_pairs"}; conflicts = land cells with more than one claimant; smaller Cliopatria Area wins; _conflicts.csv has (year, slug_a=winner, slug_b=loser, cells). Totals: 120,881 conflict cells over all anchors in 672 pairs (2020: 13,273 cells; 2024: 1 cell; 1600: 278). 2020 owns 517,625 of 524,441 cells across 192 polities. _report.csv (120 rows) and _areas.csv (7,361 rows: cells owned, cells claimed, cells incl. sea, cell km2, Cliopatria km2, ratio, ratio_claimed) written. Mount footprint: data/ 19 MB (anchors+CSVs 9.2 MB, land_r5.txt 8.4 MB, previews 0.95 MB).

Area ratios: median 0.951 on owned cells (0.952 on claimed); p5 0.68, p95 1.29; 116 rows under 0.5, 23 over 2. Worst: 0 for 9 rows (Seychelles 1980-2024, New France 1630, First French colonial empire 1810, British East Africa 1970: shapes smaller than a cell drawn slightly off their island), lowest non-zero 0.0008 (Kievan Rus' 1200, loses to its principalities), highest 5.79 (Kingdom of Mercia 900, 44 km2 -> one cell). The 20 worst with causes are in data/grid/README.md; causes are Cliopatria overlaps (ratio_claimed near 1), sub-cell islands, and coastline clipping (~half a cell per coast, which is why the median is 0.95).

Preview 1600: 97 polities, 184,232 cells, 49,528 vertices; 1,945,494 bytes at full precision, 811,859 bytes rounded to 3 decimals (vertex count unchanged); written as data/grid/preview_1600.geojson. PNG rendered with PIL (3600x1500 equirectangular, one fill per polity, 135,369 bytes); matplotlib and cairo are not installed.

Run time of the full compile: land 16 s, feature cache 9 s, per-shape cells 37 s wall (two workers), anchors 8.6 s, preview 3 s; about 75 s end to end, single-process peak well under 2 GB.
problems: The master plan's land count (214,699 res-5 cells, 253 km2 each, and the res-4/res-6 figures beside it) is wrong by 2.4x: the real res-5 land grid is 524,441 cells (134.3 M km2 by h3.cell_area). Storage and res-6 estimates (would be ~3.7 M cells) should be redone.
land_r5.txt was rewritten once at 02:24 (island centroid cells added, count 524,019 -> 524,441); any builder that read it before then must re-read, since anchor indices refer to the current file.

Cliopatria overlaps that the smaller-Area rule resolves but research agents must fix: French Fifth Republic 1961-2023 is one shape that still contains Algeria (8,845 conflict cells at every anchor 1970-2020); 'Great Britain' 1969-2023 includes Oman (1,440 cells); Netherlands Antilles 1877-2023 includes Suriname (541 cells); Kievan Rus' 1040-1235 is alive beside its principalities (it keeps 4-6 cells); Brandenburg-Prussia beside Kingdom of Prussia (1710); Blue Horde beside Golden Horde (6,581 cells, 1400); Chinese Communist Party 1938-45 overlaps the USSR (5,560 cells, 1940); Kingdom of Norway and Nazi Germany both drawn in 1940; Mughal Empire 1811-56 beside the British Empire; Denmark-Norway dated 1864-1921; Sultanate of Malacca alive 1600-1630 overlapping Mataram; Kingdom of Axum 600 overlapping a Himyarite row. The 2024 rows are a clean snapshot (1 conflict cell), unlike the 2023-ending rows.

Tiny island shapes drawn off their island give zero cells: Seychelles 1976-2023 (shape 0.1 deg west of Mahe), 'Saint Kitts' 1967-2023 is drawn at Saint Croix, 'New France' 1629-31 and 'New Netherland' 1800-02 are Saint Martin; 9 (year, slug) rows have 0 cells.

The smaller-Area-wins rule hands a cell to the more specific polity, which is right for components but wrong when the stale aggregate is the one that should vanish; the rendering phase needs the dossiers to delete the stale rows rather than rely on this rule.
Lakes count as land cells (ne_50m_land has no lake holes); the Caspian is excluded. If lakes should be sea, subtract ne_50m_lakes in land_cells.

Coastline clipping: a coastal cell is land only when its centre is on land, so every shape loses about half a cell per coast; median ratio 0.95, archipelagos 0.7-0.8. Display should clip the hex polygons to the coastline as the plan says.

cells_to_geojson rounding to 3 decimals halves the bytes but merges no vertices; a 2020 preview (192 polities, 517k cells) would be roughly 2-3 MB at 3 decimals, so per-era display chunks need simplification or compaction beyond rounding.

Other builders importing tools/slug.py or grid.py leave tools/__pycache__ on the mount; run python with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 (I removed the one I created; the one present now, 02:27, is another builder's).
matplotlib and cairo are not installed; the PNG used PIL. ijson is not installed either, so the 173 MB GeoJSON is parsed with json.load once (about 2 GB peak) into the pickle cache.

gazetteer.summary: Gazetteer v0 built from Natural Earth 10m (admin-0, admin-1, rivers/lake centrelines, lakes, populated places) onto the existing H3 r5 land grid; all cells are run-encoded indices into data/grid/land_r5.txt. Files: countries.jsonl 257 rows (522,371 cells; 6 micro-states moved to nearest land cell, 10 ocean specks with none), admin1.jsonl 4,588 rows (522,988 cells; NE "region" grouping field kept; 127 moved, 87 island/city units without a cell), rivers.jsonl 1,053 named rivers (43,497 cells), lakes.jsonl 725 (4,756 cells), places.jsonl 7,714 (7,342 NE + 372 historical cities from knowledge; 46 null cells), regions.jsonl 725 historical regions {name, alt_names, spec, confidence, note} (confidence 3: 330, 2: 344, 1: 51; 86 use polygons), generated by tools/regions_src.py which keeps hand-added rows. tools/gazetteer.py resolves the full master-plan grammar (country, admin1 incl. NE region values, place+km with optional country, lon/lat, cliopatria via grid.py/anchors, region, polygon, border_band, union/minus/intersect) plus river/lake extensions, with normalised names, alias tables, exact-name-before-alias ranking, and GazetteerError messages listing the closest matches; CLI: resolve '<json>' [--cells], check [--counts], names <text>. `check`: 725/725 regions resolve, 0 empty, 0 failed. Resolved counts: Khorasan 2,206 cells (~558,000 km2), Normandy 129, Deccan 3,081, Hexi Corridor 842. README documents schemas, counts, grammar, matching rules, how to add a region, and known gaps. Two resolver bugs found and fixed during checking: a place spec carrying "country" resolved to the whole country (dispatch order), and an alias with a parenthesised suffix could shadow an exact region name (Great Lakes).
problems: Natural Earth files Crimea and Sevastopol under Russia: {"admin1":"Crimea","country":"Ukraine"} fails with 'found in: Russia'; the Crimea region uses the Russian rows.

Country rows include overseas parts (Netherlands Caribbean municipalities, French overseas departments, Canaries, Azores/Madeira, Svalbard, Easter Island, Galapagos, Alaska/Hawaii); regions 'European Netherlands' and 'Metropolitan France' exist, other cases need an explicit minus.

86 of 725 regions rely on hand-drawn polygons (Hexi Corridor, Tarim Basin, Ordos, steppe, desert and American frontier regions); their edges are approximate and carry confidence 1-2; 51 regions are confidence 1 guesses.

NE spelling quirks and typos are kept as unit names (Seien-et-Marne, Zinguldak, Kinkkale, Crotene, Oristrano, Sjaaelland); aliases cover common ones only. Greek 'Attiki' sits in NE region 'Peloponnisos'; Quneitra (Golan) is a sliver, so Golan is a polygon.
Regions resolve to present-day land cells (today's coastlines, Aral Sea); rivers are 1,053 NE 10m centrelines without smaller tributaries; lakes under ~250 km2 are one cell or none.

372 knowledge-sourced places have no population and coordinates to about 0.05 degrees; 46 NE places (Antarctic stations, atolls) have no land cell. Wikidata/OSM were unreachable so names could not be cross-checked.
tools/regions_src.py keeps regions.jsonl rows it does not define, so a renamed region leaves a stale row until deleted by hand (one such row, the old African 'Great Lakes', was deleted this run).
tools/__pycache__ holds grid/slug bytecode written by Python imports (pre-existing, left in place).

colours.summary: Colour registry and tools published. colours.json holds: rules (space oklab, oklab_min_distance 0.10 with why; neighbour and lifetime rules; vassal = OKLCH chroma x0.55 and lightness +0.12 with own outline and label; occupied = owner's fill with the occupier's colour hatched at 45 deg; contested = OKLab midpoint of the two claimants plus a fine hatch; rebel; neutral nobody's-land warm grey #d6d0c9 = oklch(0.86 0.012 75); culture = chroma x0.40, lightness +0.15, dotted fill; expansion_outline, label, basemap), families (29: rome, china, china-division, steppe, mongol, persia, hellenistic, caliphate, islam-west, britain, france, germany, austria, iberia, portugal, italy, nordic, russia, east-europe, balkans, india, japan, korea, southeast-asia, americas, pacific, africa, egypt, near-east; each {hue: [start, end] degrees, note}), wheel (24 hues every 15 deg x light L0.80/C0.10, mid L0.70/C0.12, deep L0.58/C0.13 = 72 colours, chroma clipped to sRGB, ids like h120-mid), fixed (415 entries for 227 conventional states counting a group as one; Cliopatria rows of one state share a group and a colour: thirteen French regimes blue, Rome red / Western Rome crimson-orange / Byzantium Tyrian purple, Han vermilion, Tang gold, Song teal-green, Ming deep red, Qing imperial yellow, PRC vermilion-red, caliphates green, Persia teal, Russia dark green, Ottomans olive, USSR deep red, Japan deep crimson, etc.; every moved colour carries a note saying why), assigned (1,129 remaining leaf polities coloured from the wheel by greedy graph colouring over the union of all 120 anchor years' H3-edge adjacency plus the polity table's 25 km lifetime neighbours, largest first, lightness variant by crowding: deep 439, mid 560, light 130, 0 short), assigned_meta and log. Minimum distance 0.10 OKLab, chosen by measurement: about five JNDs; Tableau 10's closest pair is 0.084; wheel hues 15 deg apart are 0.025-0.038, 60 deg apart 0.10-0.13, lightness variants 0.10-0.12 apart, so 0.10 means a different hue family or a clearly different lightness; the wheel holds 17 mutually distinct colours at 0.10 (22 at 0.08, 10 at 0.12); greedy colouring clears 0.10 for all 1,129 polities and 0.12 for all but 3 but fails 43 at 0.14; the conventional palette would lose 57 neighbouring pairs at 0.12; every colour keeps >= 0.107 from the neutral grey and 0.18 from the pale basemap; the vassal tint sits 0.12-0.15 from its suzerain. check result (run in place from the mount against data/anchors): 120 anchor years, 12,401 neighbouring year-pairs, 0 pairs below 0.10, 14 same-group pairs (intended), 0 uncoloured polities, exit 0; ring-2 (two cells apart, across straits) 12,805 year-pairs, also 0 clashes; synthetic test (400 polities, 1,768 edges, max degree 14) 0 short, 0 clashes. seed also warns when two contemporary states are closer than 0.02 (none; 82 pairs sit between 0.02 and 0.03 and never touch). colour.py commands: seed, assign, check [--min --year --ring --all --json --anchors DIR], set SLUG HEX --note (refuses clashes, logs), show, swatch, synthetic, and distance/blend/tint/oklch/hex on the command line; the library exports distance, blend, tint, contested, hex_to_oklab/oklab_to_hex, hex_to_oklch/oklch_to_hex, load_registry, colour_of. colours-README.md explains the files, the structure, how the colours were chosen, the commands, and that the colour agent changes a colour only through check -> set --note -> check, never by hand and never in a window file.
problems: Adjacency is sampled at the 120 anchor years plus the polity table's 25 km neighbour spans; a border that exists only between anchors is covered by the second source but not checked year by year until the compiled windows exist (check --anchors DIR can then be pointed at them).

Cliopatria artefacts create some neighbour pairs the palette had to clear anyway: the Tianjin concessions put Austria-Hungary, Japan, Italy and Russia side by side in 1910; the Kingdom of Italy row runs 587..1946; the Chinese Communist Party row of 1938-45 overlaps the USSR. When the research agents split such rows, each new slug needs a fixed entry (set, or colour_seed.py then seed --force and assign).
check compares full colours only: a vassal tint against a neighbour's full colour, or two contested blends side by side, is not checked; the hatch and outline carry that case.
assign recolours every non-fixed polity from scratch for a given anchor set, so it is a Phase A tool; once windows are compiled, colours change only through set.
82 contemporary (never neighbouring) pairs of fixed states are 0.02..0.03 apart in OKLab (e.g. Rome and Han both red, Sweden and Romania blues); cosmetic, reported as a count by seed.

Caches (H3 neighbour table, per-anchor adjacency, seed neighbours) and the swatch sheet live under /tmp/claude-0/work/colours/ and are rebuilt automatically when missing or stale; the mount holds no cache.

spec.summary: Wrote the dossier schema (JSON Schema 2020-12, additionalProperties false at the top level, a description on every field, the shared region grammar as $defs/region with the gazetteer's river/lake extensions, if/then rules for corrections, regions and counterparts), the validator tools/validate_dossier.py (uses jsonschema 4.26 when importable, otherwise a built-in checker for the subset the schema uses; plus file-name/slug, year-order, source-listing, keyframe-coverage against data/shapes.csv, start/end pairing, certainty-coverage checks, and --resolve through tools/gazetteer.py, --json for counts), the worked Tang example polities/_example-tang-dynasty.json built from 19 opened Wikipedia pages (the ten named plus Guiyi Circuit, Silla-Tang War, Andong, Eastern Turkic Khaganate, Anbei, Beiting, Tuyuhun, Later Liang, the emperor list), the five briefs (research, reviewer, window, colour, gazetteer) as Markdown templates with {{placeholders}}, and briefs/README.md listing them with the per-brief placeholder table and the fill procedure. The example validates: 0 errors, 2 benign warnings (Nanzhao and Guiyi vassalages that last to 907); 60 ledger events (20 gain, 13 loss, 7 vassal_start, 5 vassal_end, 3 contest_start, 3 contest_end, 3 capital_move, 2 rename, 1 occupation pair, 1 found, 1 dissolve; 2 at confidence 1), 19 sources, 33 keyframe verdicts (32 Cliopatria shapes: 9 ok, 23 adjust; plus 1 new keyframe for 618-622), 11 wars, 4 capitals, 24 rulers, 220 region specs all resolving through the gazetteer. The validator fails a deliberately broken copy with 12 precise errors and works with jsonschema hidden. Scratch under /tmp/claude-0/work/briefs/; no temporary files left on the mount; nothing else in history/ touched.
problems: Cliopatria has 32 Tang shapes (data/polities.csv n_shapes=32, 32 rows in shapes.csv), not the 47 the task text and master-plan.md state; the master plan's figure should be corrected.

Cliopatria's Tang row needs the corrections recorded in the example's keyframe_review: it starts 623 instead of 618 and ends 910 instead of 907 with successors starting 911; the Sui row runs to 627; the Mongolian Plateau is drawn as direct Tang land 633-681 (Xueyantuo until 645, jimi protectorate after 647); the 661-673 shapes reach 58 E (Khorasan); Hexi and the Western Regions are removed in 757 although Liangzhou fell in 764 and Kucha in 787; the Guiyi Circuit's Hexi (848-907) is given to 'Tibetans' and 'Ganzhou Kingdom'.

Cliopatria lacks states the Tang ledger needs as counterparts: An Lushan's Yan (756-763) and Huang Chao's Qi (881-884) as type rebel, the Xueyantuo, the Kingdom of Gaochang, the Guiyi Circuit; the research brief's 'states Cliopatria lacks' rule covers them and the example's notes list suggested slugs.
Probable label swap in Cliopatria to check (Inner Asia group): 'Türgesh' 692-749 lies in Mongolia and 'Turks' 666-756 in Kazakhstan/Kyrgyzstan.

Pages disagree on four dates, recorded in the example's notes: Tuyuhun's fall to Tibet 663 (Tibetan Empire page) vs 670 (Tuyuhun infobox); Emperor Ai's deposition 12 May 907 (emperor list) vs the abdication of 1 June 907 (Tang page, Later Liang infobox); Wu Zetian's proclamation 16 vs 17 October 690; Nanzhao's break with the Tang 750, 751 or 754.

WebFetch gaps: the 'Beiting Protectorate' page is a stub with no dates (790 for Beiting is at confidence 1); 'Tang campaign against Tuyuhun' returned URL_NOT_FOUND (the Tuyuhun page was used instead); the Tang dynasty page does not date the southern conquests of 618-628 (Xiao Xian, Fu Gongshi), so the 623 shape stands with a note that 'Transition from Sui to Tang' should be opened by a gap-filler; the 'Anxi Protectorate' URL resolves to the same article as 'Protectorate General to Pacify the West'.
The gazetteer has no place entries for Jiuquan (Suzhou) or Guazhou; the example uses a coordinate radius for Jiuquan and widens Dunhuang's radius for Guazhou; the gazetteer agent should add both.

Design choices the orchestrator may want to confirm: the window brief specifies compiled/<window>.json with the task's keys (window, years{changes[cells,from,to,status], contests, captions}, handoff) plus optional suzerain/occupier/claimants/event fields, a capitals list and handoff open-relation lists, assumes the Phase C anchors keep data/anchors' {year, owners} format, and tells the first window agent to write one shared tools/compile_window.py that the other 118 reuse.

Schema extensions beyond the task's field list, all described: optional 'source' and 'note' on capitals and rulers, optional from/to/note on keyframe entries (new keyframes require from/to), optional '$schema' at the top level, and the river/lake region forms that tools/gazetteer.py already resolves; the counterpart of vassal_start/vassal_end is defined as the vassal itself so the validator can pair them (the example was adjusted to match).
validate_dossier.py --resolve takes about 15 s per dossier because {cliopatria} specs load grid.py's Cliopatria feature cache; acceptable, but a batch of hundreds should run in one process.
